key_insight: UniT introduces a unified physical language—latent action tokens anchored to visual consequences—that bridges the kinematic gap between human egocentric data and humanoid control, enabling effective human-to-humanoid policy transfer and world modeling.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of robot-collected data and the cross-embodiment challenge: how to reuse abundant egocentric human data for humanoid policy learning despite mismatched kinematics.
method: Unified Latent Action Tokenizer: compress heterogeneous motion/control into a shared discrete/continuous token space representing physical actions.
Visual Anchoring: align human and humanoid behaviors via shared visual consequences (egocentric observations) rather than direct joint-to-joint mapping.
Dual-use tokens: use the unified tokens both to train humanoid policies (action decoding) and to build world models (predictive latent dynamics) for planning and simulation.
impact: Enables scaling humanoid foundation models using large-scale human video datasets, reducing dependence on scarce robotic data and improving transferability and sample efficiency for downstream control and simulation tasks.

paper_title: UniT: Toward a Unified Physical Language for Human-to-Humanoid Policy Learning and World Modeling
paper_authors: Boyu Chen, Yi Chen, Lu Qiu, Jerry Bai, Yuying Ge
